Subject: Dedicated capacity guidance — heavy long-context & mixed latency workload

Hi Sean,

Thanks for taking the meeting yesterday. I attached our anonymized inference profile (stonebridge-inference-profile.csv) but quick summary: we run a mix of real-time conversational agents (latency-sensitive, 99th <= 200ms target), large long-context retrieval-augmented generation jobs (models in the 70B parameter class with 32k+ context, heavy KV-cache usage), and high-throughput batched analytics for embeddings. Typical peak: ~1.2k concurrent chat sessions with 5–10 turns each and intermittent batch windows that need sustained token throughput (~8–12k tokens/sec).

Primary asks:
- What Dedicated SKU mix do you recommend (H100 vs A100 vs L4) for a cost-effective, SLA-backed deployment?
- Ops checklist for initial pilot vs production (autoscale, prewarm, cache sizing, fallbacks).
- Any quantization/tiling recommendations to save slots without affecting 99th latency too much.

We're also evaluating Reserved vs Reserved+Burst. Procurement would like a one-pager with SKU counts and an estimated monthly committed cost we can take to finance.

Attachments: stonebridge-inference-profile.csv (CSV, 38 KB)

Best,
Eva
Head of Platform
Stonebridge AI

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity guidance — heavy long-context & mixed latency workload

Hi Eva — thanks for the profile. Forwarding an initial, pragmatic recommendation so procurement has something concrete for planning; Ben and Dev are looped for commercial and ops detail.

Top-level recommendation (pilot -> prod):
1) Pilot (2–3 weeks spike test): small mixed pool to validate tiling and cache hit rates
   - 2 x H100 (80GB) dedicated slots for long-context model pilot (prewarmed, KV pinned)
   - 4 x A100 (40GB) for mid-tier generation and fallbacks
   - 6 x L4 (24GB) for embeddings and low-latency routing

2) Production baseline (initial commit) — scaled by expected concurrency and headroom
   - H100s: 6 slots — primary for long-context, continuous KV cache residency, and batched throughput windows
   - A100s: 12 slots — balanced generation, can host quantized 70B variants and mid-size models
   - L4s: 20 slots — cost-effective for embeddings, light chat, and burst lanes (low per-token cost)

Rationale and tradeoffs:
- H100 (80GB) = best for memory-bound, long-context models where KV cache and larger activation memory prevent tiling; reduces tail latency for heavy sessions.
- A100 (40GB) = best tradeoff for many production gen workloads — supports 70B quantized variants with modest tiling; good throughput per-dollar for mid-weight models.
- L4 (24GB) = low-cost, low-latency for embeddings and smaller chat models; where accuracy tolerance allows quantized lower-memory variants.

Operational notes (short):
- Reserve KV cache residency on H100s for top X% of sessions (session affinity policy).
- Autoscaling: keep fast warm pool on L4s for sub-100ms routing; autoscale A100s for throughput; H100s should be mostly reserved with limited burst policies.
- Quantization: use 4-bit/8-bit where model fidelity allows; bank A100s with quantized variants and keep H100s for FP16 when fidelity matters.

I'll work with Dev and Soojin to turn this into an ops checklist and a quoted MSRP for a 12-month reserved commitment + 20% burst. Ben will follow up on commercial terms.

Attachments to follow: proposed-sku-matrix.xlsx, ops-checklist-dedicated.txt

Cheers,
Sean
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Forwarding Sean's note — comments below for the quote and upstream procurement ask.

Ben's internal notes:
- Commercial framing: propose a 12-month Reserved (commit) with 6 H100 / 12 A100 / 18 L4 as a standard package; include a 30% discount on L4 if they commit to a usage floor for embeddings.
- Billing cadence: monthly, with an agreed-upon overage rate for burst usage beyond 20% of reserved capacity.
- PO path: procurement will want clear metrics we will hit — define SLOs (99th latency for chat, sustained batch throughput) and a pilot acceptance test (two full spike windows).

Dev's ops notes (inline):
- Prewarm & tiling: ensure models that need 32k context are tested with our continuous-batch tiling mode; prewarm pipelines on H100s to keep KV caches hot.
- Fault isolation: put H100-backed long-context sessions behind a dedicated route with automatic fallback to A100 quantized variant if H100 capacity is constrained (with degraded fidelity notice).
- Cache sizing: recommend reserve ~1.2x nominal KV footprint on H100 pool to avoid eviction during peak.
- Observability: add per-route token-cost dashboards, 99th-latency alerts, and regeneration counters to the console before pilot sign-off.

I'll draft a short quote and attach the proposed-sku-matrix.xlsx and ops-checklist-dedicated.txt to the outbound.

-Ben

Hi Eva — attaching a concise pilot proposal and ops checklist. Summary below and next steps.

Pilot summary (2 weeks):
- Provision: 2 H100 / 4 A100 / 6 L4 reserved for pilot window.
- Acceptance criteria: two 6-hour spike windows with
  * chat 99th latency <= 200ms on L4/A100 routing for sub-750 concurrent sessions
  * long-context flows executed on H100 with KV-hit >= 85% and no >2s tail events
  * batch throughput >= 8k tokens/sec for sustained 30-minute windows

Production recommendation (initial commit):
- Baseline reserved pool: 6 H100 / 12 A100 / 20 L4.
- Autoscale policy: L4 autoscale with sub-minute scale-up; A100 scale on queue depth and token backlog; H100 reserved with 10% burst allowance (paid).
- Fallbacks: route overflow to quantized A100 variants; if overall capacity constrained, degrade to shorter context mode and notify app via header.
- Quantization plan: test 4-bit quantization for non-critical paths on A100s; keep H100s for FP16/FP32 slices.

Operational checklist (ops-checklist-dedicated.txt attached):
- Prewarm models and pin KV caches on H100s before pilot start time
- Configure per-route routing policies and SLOs in console
- Set up telemetry dashboards: per-model token cost, tail-latency percentiles, cache miss rate
- Canary strategy: 5% canary traffic on A100 quantized variant for 48 hours before full rollout
- Autoscaling thresholds and burn-in windows documented

Attachments: proposed-sku-matrix.xlsx (xlsx, 56 KB), ops-checklist-dedicated.txt (txt, 6 KB)

Next steps:
1) Procurement to confirm financial cadence and PO path.
2) Agree pilot date (we can spin infra in 48 hours once PO is in).
3) Run spike test and capture dashboards for sign-off.

If that looks good I'll get a formal quote out today; Ben will follow up on discount tiers.

Best,
